title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary on most days. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Mixed

The major indices started the day on a positive note but struggled to hold gains, experiencing a sharp sell-off following news of new U.S. tariffs on key trade partners, including Mexico, Canada, and China. This added to the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, keeping volatility elevated, as has been the case since late last year.

Despite today’s selling pressure, the major indices are still holding near key moving averages (10-, 20-, and 50-day MAs). Internals remain slightly positive, with breadth and momentum holding up, though not by a wide margin. Sector trends remain mostly intact, but given today’s distribution, it’s critical to monitor whether key levels hold or if further weakness emerges. Continued distribution in the indices and a break below these levels would be a negative signal and could shift the market environment back into a more defensive stance.

For now, while conditions remain mixed, the market is still at a pivotal juncture. If support holds, this could be a temporary shakeout, but if selling intensifies and internals weaken further, caution will be warranted. As we look to see which scenario plays out, keep your powder dry, cash levels high, and only add exposure on the heels of positive price action in your stocks.

Index Trends: Negative

  • Large Cap: Positive

Overall Up/Down Momentum: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Positive

  • Small Cap: Negative

Plan of Action

Focus on Capital Preservation and High-Quality Opportunities

  • Selective Entry on New Trades: The market environment remains mixed, with indices holding key levels but facing increased volatility and distribution following tariff-related headlines. While some sector trends remain intact, uncertainty remains high. Focus on high-probability setups that demonstrate clear relative strength, tight consolidations, or clean breakouts with strong volume. Given the current conditions, probing trades cautiously is still an option, but avoid aggressive positioning and chasing extended moves.

  • Start Small on New Trades: The risk of further downside remains, so it’s critical to start with smaller positions and scale up only if trades show strong follow-through and resilience. This flexibility allows for quick adjustments if market conditions deteriorate.

Monitor Market Internals for Further Clarity

  • Track Breadth and Momentum: Internals remain slightly positive but have weakened under the surface due to today’s selling pressure. Monitor whether downside breadth expands further or stabilizes. If new highs contract while new lows expand, it could signal increased risk.

  • Be Mindful of Reversal Risks: The recent internal improvement is being tested as indices struggle to hold above key moving averages. If the major indices violate key levels (10-, 20-, 50-day MAs) or downside momentum accelerates, reduce exposure accordingly.

Stay Flexible and Proactively Manage Risk

  • Use Reasonable Stops: Given the renewed selling pressure, tighten stop-losses where necessary while ensuring they are not so tight that normal market fluctuations take you out of otherwise solid setups.

  • Adjust Cash Levels Dynamically: With increased volatility and sector rotation, keeping a healthy cash buffer is advisable. This ensures flexibility if conditions worsen while allowing for quick action when quality setups emerge.

  • Scale Exposure Gradually: If indices rebound from key moving averages and internals stabilize, cautiously increase exposure. If breakdowns persist and distribution increases, be prepared to scale back aggressively.

Reassess Market Conditions Daily

  • Evaluate Continuously: The market remains fluid and news-driven, requiring daily assessment of breadth, momentum, and index trends. Watch closely for signs of stabilization or further deterioration.

  • Adapt Exposure Responsively: If market internals firm up and key levels hold, selectively increase exposure to high-quality setups. If weakness persists or major indices lose key support, reduce exposure accordingly.

Key Focus

  • Patience and Discipline: The market is still at a pivotal juncture—while some setups are forming, volatility remains high. Avoid overcommitting capital until stronger confirmation emerges.

  • Anticipate Volatility: With tariff-related headlines and geopolitical uncertainties, expect continued market swings. Managing risk carefully and staying flexible will be key to navigating this phase effectively.

Bottom Line:

The market is still holding key levels but faces renewed distribution pressure. Maintain a cautious approach, focusing on relative strength, risk management, and daily reassessment. Be ready to scale exposure up if stability returns—or cut back if conditions worsen.
